messages.subject: Question MCDS - re-post
parts:
Hello list,

A couple of weeks ago I posted the following message, but I did not receive
any reply. Considering a strange error warning which I got shortly after
sending the message, I wonder if it was correctly distributed to the list.
For this reason I re-post it, hoping that someone could answer my questions,=

at least only by pointing me to the relevant documentation which I
eventually missed.

Thanks,

Dimitri




Hello,

I have a probably stupid question regarding the estimate of the detection
function at multiple levels in MCDS engine.

I am analysing data of bird transect counts in Italy. My design consists of
40 transects randomly distributed within 2 strata, which strongly differ
regarding both birds=92 density and detectability, visited in two different
seasons during one year. Among the others, the objective of my study is to
estimate bird population size before and after the breeding season.
Given the current limit of Distance regarding nested design, I construct a
model using season as covariate and fitting separate detection functions for=

each stratum.
My problem is that Distance estimates density at three different levels,
i.e. global, stratum and sample (transects), while I'm interested in density=

estimates at covariate (season) level. Probably I missed something, but I
read Buckland et al. (2001) and the on-line documentation of Distance 5.0
(especially chapter 9 - Estimating the detection function at multiple
levels) and I could not find any clue regarding the possibility to obtain
density estimates at covariate level.

My questions are:
1) Is my approach completely wrong? I.e., should I analyse the data
regarding the two strata separately using CDS, and then combine the
estimates by hand?

2) Is it possible to obtain stratum and global density estimates at
covariate levels using the above mentioned model?

I appreciate any suggestions.

Thanks,

Dimitri

messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: Question MCDS - re-post
parts:
Dimitri-

I didn't see your earlier post.

In the current implementation of Distance you cannot do what you want to=20
do with the code. You will be able to do it in future versions.
For the time being I suggest that you do the following. Redefine your 2=20
strata into 4. Region 1 season 1, region 1 season 2, region 2 season 1=20
and region 2 season 2.
Fit your mcds model using season, region and whaever other covariates=20
are relevant. Then get your density output by stratum and then combine=20
the strata within a season in a spreadsheet.
The point estimate is straightforward and the variance requires a little=20
more work but you'll find the formulas in the book. It may require a=20
little thinking depending on what covariates are used.
If you only use season as an mcds covariate then it is straightforward=20
to combine the strata within season using the formulas in the book.=20
However, when you then want to compare seasonal densitites they will=20
covary and you'll have to work out the covariance. That is the trickier=20
aspect to the programming that I'm working on for future versions.

--jeff
